title: Mara and the Asset
premise: Sebastian Eriksen, a burned-out private security contractor, is approached by Mara Voss, a stranger who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. She needs his help extracting her brother Anton, an intelligence analyst defecting from a private intelligence syndicate whose leaked data could crater European markets when Frankfurt opens in seventy-two hours. As Sebastian and Mara run the extraction across Copenhagen and the Baltic coast, Sebastian realizes Anton may be deliberate bait to flush out a mole inside Sebastian's own firm, and that Mara's debt story is itself a cover for something older between them. In the end Sebastian chooses truth over loyalty to his employer, exposes the mole at the moment of handoff, and escapes with Anton's data — and with Mara — though the cost is his old life burned behind him.
about_author: Yara Halloran is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms she cannot name. She now writes thrillers from a coastal town in Denmark, where she insists the fog does the editing.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet him mid-contract in Copenhagen: polished lies, packed bag, a firm that guards clients nobody trusts. A routine protection job goes subtly wrong when he spots surveillance that isn't aimed at his client. Emotional beat: restless unease, the sense his careful life is already over.

chapters.title: A Favor Never Given
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A woman intercepts Sebastian outside his apartment, thanking him for saving her life in Riga three years ago — an operation he never worked. She leaves a keycard and a time. Emotional beat: magnetic disorientation; Sebastian can't decide if she's a con or a summons.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He checks the Riga file: someone scrubbed his name into records he was never part of. Whoever built this lie wanted him reachable — and deniable. He decides to hear Mara out before his employers do. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding professional caution.

chapters.title: Anton
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a safehouse flat, Mara explains: her brother Anton, an analyst for the Halvard Syndicate, has data that will move markets at Frankfurt open. He wants out; the Syndicate wants him used as bait. She needs a contractor the Syndicate doesn't own. Emotional beat: desperate candor masking a hidden agenda.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian negotiates terms while privately running background on Mara — and finds her identity is real but shallow, three years deep, exactly as long as the Riga lie. He takes the job anyway. Emotional beat: complicity; he chooses the mystery knowingly.

chapters.title: The Firm
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His employer, Kestrel Risk Group, assigns him a parallel task: identify the leak inside their own operation. His handler, Ilse Brandt, watches him too closely. Emotional beat: the trap tightening — he is now working both sides of one question.

chapters.title: Copenhagen Rain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Recon of Anton's handler's route through Nyhavn. Mara and Sebastian work well together — too well — and a near-miss with Syndicate watchers forces them to improvise as a couple. Emotional beat: intimacy growing under operational cover.

chapters.title: Signal Traffic
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian decrypts intercepted traffic suggesting the Syndicate expects the extraction — and that Kestrel's leak is feeding them. Someone inside his firm wants Anton taken, but not rescued. Emotional beat: cold dread replacing adrenaline.

chapters.title: What Mara Knows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback thread: the real event behind the Riga fabrication — Sebastian did save someone, years ago, and Mara has been hunting the truth of it since. She hasn't told him everything. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Handler's Dinner
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian gets close to Anton's Syndicate handler at a restaurant meet, confirming the extraction window and learning the Syndicate's counter-plan runs through Kestrel. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his employer may be the enemy's instrument.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tails Ilse Brandt and photographs a dead-drop exchange — proof of the mole, but ambiguous about which side Ilse serves. Mara must decide whether to show Sebastian, knowing what it reveals about her own omissions. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts Mara with what he's pieced together; she finally shows him the Riga truth. The fight is quiet and devastating — then they rebuild the plan together on honest ground. Emotional beat: love against duty, chosen explicitly.

chapters.title: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Planning montage: routes to the Baltic, a boat, forged papers, Frankfurt deadline math. Kestrel reassigns Sebastian away from Copenhagen — a move that confirms everything. He burns his go-bag contents and goes dark. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Burns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Syndicate shooters hit the safehouse minutes after they leave; Anton is moved early to a fallback neither planned for. Mara realizes only one person knew the fallback. Emotional beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian decodes the Syndicate traffic fully: Anton was always the lure, and the true target is the mole handoff at the Baltic marina — where Kestrel plans to sell Anton back. The extraction was never the mission; the frame-up was. Emotional beat: clarity at the worst hour.

chapters.title: Crossing the Sound
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Night crossing by boat toward the marina handoff, evading a patrol cutter. Anton, retrieved en route, is brittle and brilliant, insisting the data goes public regardless of whether he survives. Emotional beat: fragile trust among three people with separate debts.

chapters.title: The Marina
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The handoff begins: Ilse arrives to trade Anton for the Syndicate's silence about Kestrel's own market manipulation. Sebastian walks in wearing a wire, playing the loyal contractor one last time. Emotional beat: controlled terror, the performance of a lifetime.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax part one: Sebastian springs the exposure — broadcasting Ilse's deal to both Syndicate and Kestrel leadership simultaneously, turning each side on the other. Gunfire breaks the marina open. Emotional beat: the choice made irreversible.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. As dawn hits Europe, Anton's data releases and markets convulse; the Syndicate's leverage dies mid-transaction. In the chaos, Mara covers Sebastian's escape, taking a wound that isn't fatal but isn't nothing. Emotional beat: triumph laced with blood.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Copenhagen
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Kestrel collapses into scandal; Ilse vanishes, leaving a note that suggests she was also playing a longer game. Sebastian is professionally dead and, for the first time, unafraid of it. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: The Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tells Sebastian the last truth: there was no favor owed — she invented the debt because it was the only door she could build into his locked-down life. He forgives her not despite the lie but because of what she built with it. Emotional beat: belonging earned honestly.

chapters.title: New Papers, Same People
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing chapter. Weeks later: new names, a small harbor town, Anton rebuilding his life in witness-quiet. A Kestrel remnant makes one last approach and is turned away without a shot. Sebastian unpacks the go-bag for good. Emotional beat: resolution — home as a choice, not a cover.
